guideTitle: Best TV Stands for 55 Inch TVs (2026)
metaTitle: Best TV Stands for 55 Inch TVs (2026)
metaDescription: Five TV stands for 55 inch TVs compared on length, depth, storage, cable access and foot spacing, with honest notes on particleboard, outlets and tip over risk.
expertTake: The Faesun 55.1 in console is our top pick because its length, curved edges and two fabric drawers suit a 55 inch TV and a small family room. The JARHETUN three tier steel frame stand is the value pick when you only need open shelves for a console and a soundbar. Skip any stand under about 48 in long unless you have confirmed your TV feet sit close together.
introParagraphs: The inch label on a TV is a diagonal, and the width of the set is what decides whether a stand fits. Listings say a stand fits a given screen size, but the real fit depends on the distance between the TV feet, the depth of the stand top and the load rating. A stand that is a few inches too narrow leaves the feet hanging off the edge.

Most stands in this size range are particleboard or MDF with a laminate finish, built on metal or wood legs. The real differences are length, storage layout, cable access and whether the piece includes anti tip hardware. This guide compares five stands on those points for a mid size television.

products.name: Faesun 55.1 in TV Stand, Curved Edges, Two Fabric Drawers
products.description:
The Faesun measures 55.1 by 15.7 by 21.6 in and is listed for 50, 55 and 60 inch TVs. The 55 in length leaves about 3 in of margin on each side of a 48 in wide TV, which is the comfortable range for most feet positions. The curved edges soften corners that a child or a passing adult might clip, and the two fabric drawers swallow remotes, cables and controllers.

The tradeoff is depth. At 15.7 in, the top is shallow, so a TV with feet set far forward may overhang slightly, and a soundbar plus a TV on a narrow top can feel cramped. Compared with the PRAISUN, it has no built in power outlets, so you need a surge strip behind it. The JARHETUN is shorter and has fewer enclosed spaces.

In a real room it needs a wall with at least 60 in of clear width, plus a few inches to each side for cord access. Fabric drawers are lighter than wood and can sag if overloaded, so keep them to remotes and media. Expect assembly with two people for an hour or so, and re tighten the fasteners after the first month.
products.bestFor: Families who want a roomy top, soft corners and hidden storage for small items.
pros: 55.1 in length leaves margin around a 55 in TV
Curved edges reduce accidental bumps
Two drawers hide remotes and cables
Open shelves fit a console or router
cons: 15.7 in depth is shallow for forward feet
No built in outlets, so you need a surge strip

products.name: JARHETUN 47.2 in Three Tier Open Shelf TV Stand with Steel Frame
products.description:
The JARHETUN is a three tier open shelf stand with an X shaped steel frame and a particleboard top, at 47.2 in long. Open shelves keep a console, cable box and router in the air and make remote signals reach the devices. The steel X frame is the structural part, and it gives the stand a lighter, industrial look than the boxy faux wood alternatives.

The tradeoff is length. A 55 inch TV is about 48 in wide, so a 47.2 in stand is shorter than the TV itself. That works only if the TV feet sit well inside the width of the stand, and you should measure foot to foot before buying. The Faesun at 55.1 in is the safer fit. Open shelves also show cable clutter, so plan for ties or a tray.

In use, it assembles in an hour or less with a screwdriver, and the open design lets you reach the back for cords. Keep heavy items on the lower tier for stability. A year in, particleboard shelves can bow under a stack of consoles, and fasteners can loosen if you move the piece.
products.bestFor: Small rooms and renters who need open shelves and a lighter look.
pros: Open shelves keep electronics ventilated
Steel X frame adds rigidity
Three tiers give room for console and media
Light enough to move to a new room
cons: 47.2 in is shorter than a 55 in TV width

products.name: PRAISUN 54 in Fluted TV Stand with Outlets, USB and Sliding Doors
products.description:
The PRAISUN is a 54 in fluted front console with two AC outlets, one USB and one USB-C port built in, and curved sliding doors. The power strip behind the doors removes the need for a separate surge protector for a TV and a console. Sliding doors save space compared with swing doors in a tight room.

The tradeoff is that doors hide the electronics and can block remote signals. Infrared remotes do not pass through solid doors, so leave the doors open or use a Bluetooth or RF remote. Closed cabinets also trap heat, so confirm there is a rear opening. It sits at the top of the price tiers in this list, and the cheaper JARHETUN has no outlets and no doors.

In a real room the 54 in length gives margin around a 48 in TV, and the outlets cut cord clutter. Plan on two people and a few hours for assembly because of the doors and wiring. Check that the built in outlets are rated for your total load, and do not daisy chain other power strips into them.
products.bestFor: Living rooms that want a clean look with power included and hidden storage.
pros: Built in outlets cut cable clutter
Sliding doors save swing space
54 in length suits a 55 in TV
Fluted front adds texture

products.name: HAPPYMONT Mid Century TV Stand for 55 and 60 in TVs, Two Cabinets
products.description:
The HAPPYMONT is a mid century stand sold for 55 and 60 inch TVs, with five supportive legs and anti scratch foot pads, two roomy cabinets and a cord control cutout. The raised legs let you see floor beneath it, which keeps a small room airy and makes it easier to clean under. The wood tone styling suits a mid century sofa and a walnut floor.

The tradeoff is that the five legs spread the load across more points, which is stable on a flat floor, but the table surface is engineered wood and can chip at the leg joints if moved. Compared with the Faesun it is more of a statement piece but has fewer open shelves for consoles. The cabinets are closed, so infrared remotes may struggle.

In a real room, keep it away from a radiator. Assembly is a two person job, and the soft closing hinges need careful alignment. Over a few years, a light veneer can scratch near the front edge, so use felt pads under objects and avoid sliding items across the top.
products.bestFor: Mid century or warm wood rooms that want a raised, tidy console.
pros: Five legs spread the load and protect floors
Raised design keeps the room airy
Two cabinets hide clutter
Cable cutout helps manage cords
cons: Closed cabinets can block IR remotes
Legs and veneer can chip if moved

products.name: Furologee Rustic Brown Open Shelf TV Stand with Mesh Shelves and Hooks
products.description:
The Furologee is a two tier open mesh stand in rustic brown, with four hooks on the side for controllers or headphones and a particleboard top over a metal frame. The listing makes the point that open shelves let electronics breathe and that cables are easy to reach. The mesh shelves also let air move around a console.

The tradeoff is that mesh shelves are not flat. Small items such as remotes and loose cables can slip through gaps, and a soundbar or console with small feet may tilt. Compared with the JARHETUN, it offers fewer tiers, and next to the PRAISUN it offers no cable management or doors. The finish reads as a casual rustic look and not a premium wood.

In use it is a light, simple piece that goes together in under an hour. Place a thin board or a mat on a mesh shelf to make it level for a console, and tighten the frame after the first month. A year in, the top finish can show rings from drinks, so keep it clear of mugs.
products.bestFor: Casual rooms that want open shelves and a place to hang controllers.
pros: Open mesh shelves keep electronics ventilated
Four hooks organize controllers and headsets
Metal frame adds rigidity
Easy to assemble in under an hour
cons: Mesh shelves let small items slip through
Particleboard top shows rings and wear

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 55 inch TV is about 48 in wide, but what matters is the distance between its feet, which can run from 30 to over 45 in. The stand top should be at least a few inches wider than the TV or the feet must fit inside. The Faesun at 55.1 in and PRAISUN at 54 in leave margin, while the 47.2 in JARHETUN needs measuring first. A common mistake is trusting the inch label on the listing.

Depth matters as much as length, because TV feet and a soundbar need space. The Faesun is 15.7 in deep, which is shallow but typical for this class. Tall TVs on a shallow top can tip forward if bumped. Use the furniture anti tip strap and anchor into a wall stud, especially if children are around.

Most stands in this class are particleboard or MDF with laminate, and the top supports a static load that the listing may not state. A 55 inch TV usually weighs well under 50 lb, but a console and speakers add up. Edges swell if wet and fasteners loosen after a move. Steel frames, like the JARHETUN X frame, add rigidity.

Open shelves ventilate electronics and pass infrared remote signals, as on the JARHETUN and Furologee. Doors hide clutter but block IR remotes and trap heat unless the back is open. The PRAISUN sliding doors and the HAPPYMONT cabinets look tidy but need an RF remote or open doors.

A back cutout or grommet keeps cords tidy, and a gap behind the stand eases cable routing. The PRAISUN includes two AC outlets and USB ports, which removes a surge strip. Without outlets you need a power strip, so budget space behind the stand.

Expect one to three hours for assembly, and two people for anything with doors. Re tighten fasteners after the first month. A stand should sit level on the floor, so use felt pads and adjust feet. Check height too, since a TV should sit with its center near eye level when seated.

howWeEvaluated.title: Listing specifications
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each stand from its length, depth, material and storage details on the Amazon listing. We did not assemble or handle any of these stands. Where a listing omitted a number, such as load rating, we said so.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit with a 55 inch TV
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stand lengths with a TV width of about 48 in and the usual rule that the top should be a few inches wider. The Faesun at 55.1 in and PRAISUN at 54 in fit best. We flagged the 47.2 in JARHETUN.

howWeEvaluated.title: Storage and cables
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at open versus closed storage, remote signal access and cable management. The PRAISUN has outlets and the JARHETUN has open shelves. We considered which layout suits a console, soundbar or router.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed recurring concerns for stands in this class, such as shelf bowing, fastener loosening, finish chipping and assembly difficulty. We did not repeat ratings. Those patterns shaped the cons.

howWeEvaluated.title: Distinct lineup
howWeEvaluated.description: We chose furniture stands only, leaving out tabletop swivel stands and rolling carts. We included five different layouts, from open frames to doors and drawers. Relative price tiers only set the order.

cards.label: In this comparison

maintenance.why: Cam locks and screws loosen as the piece settles or moves. A wobble is the first sign.
Dust builds up behind electronics. Use a dry or lightly damp cloth, and avoid soaking particleboard edges.
Cords can kink behind a stand. Do not daisy chain power strips on built in outlets.
An anti tip strap into a wall stud prevents tip over. Check that it is still tight.
Uneven floors cause wobble. Felt pads and levelers fix many issues.

faq.q: How wide should a TV stand be for a 55 inch TV?
faq.a: A 55 inch TV is about 48 in wide, so the stand should be at least 48 in and ideally 52 to 56 in. Check the distance between the TV feet, because some feet are set far apart.

faq.q: Can a 47 inch stand hold a 55 inch TV?
faq.a: Only if the TV feet sit inside the stand width. Measure the distance between feet. A TV that overhangs the stand sides looks and feels unstable.

faq.q: Do I need to anchor a TV stand?
faq.a: Yes where children or pets live. Use an anti tip strap into a wall stud for both the TV and the stand. Many stands include a strap, but read the listing.
Infrared remotes do not pass through solid doors. Leave the doors open, use an RF or Bluetooth remote or add a remote extender. Closed cabinets also need rear ventilation.
It is the norm at this tier. Edges swell if wet, and screws loosen after a move. Keep it dry and tighten hardware, and it will serve for years in a normal living room.

faq.q: How high should the TV sit?
faq.a: The center of the screen should be near eye level when seated, which is often about 42 in from the floor. A low stand puts the TV near the sofa back height and may need a taller table.
